flashcard_questions.q: What are weapons of mass destruction?
flashcard_questions.a: Weapons that cause widespread, indiscriminate damage to people and the environment.
They use living organisms or viruses to cause disease and death.

flashcard_questions.q: How do chemical weapons harm people?
flashcard_questions.a: They use toxic chemicals to burn, poison or paralyse humans.

flashcard_questions.q: What is nuclear deterrence as a defence policy?
flashcard_questions.a: Keeping nuclear weapons so other states dare not attack, for fear of retaliation.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Mutually Assured Destruction describe?
flashcard_questions.a: A nuclear conflict in which both sides would be completely destroyed.

flashcard_questions.q: Which weapons of mass destruction remain legal for some countries?
Why is it impossible to use a weapon of mass destruction only on military targets?
flashcard_questions.a: There will always be civilian victims.

flashcard_questions.q: What do utilitarians judge an action by?
flashcard_questions.a: Whether it produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number of people.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Muslim-majority country possesses nuclear weapons?
Which Bible verse do Christians cite when opposing weapons of mass destruction?
Which Christian group are pacifists who oppose all weapons of mass destruction?
Which Christian organisation campaigns for permanent nuclear disarmament?
flashcard_questions.a: The Christian Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Qur’an verse says a response to attack must be proportionate?
What did the Prophet Muhammad forbid during conflict?
Why do some Christians accept nuclear deterrence?
flashcard_questions.a: They see it as a necessary evil that keeps the peace and protects innocent lives.

notes: 15 cards: 4 term→definition (WMD, nuclear deterrence, Mutually Assured Destruction, utilitarians), 2 weapon→effect (biological, chemical), 3 belief→source (Matthew 5:9, Qur’an 16:126, Muhammad on civilians), 3 tradition→position (Quakers, Christian CND, Christians who accept deterrence), 3 fact/argument cards (legal status, Pakistan, civilian victims). Dropped 'sanctity of life' — it is defined in several sister lessons and would interfere here.
